subsystems.name: Active payload
subsystems.role: molecules that alter DNA methylation and histone marks to shift skin cells toward a youthful epigenetic state.
parts: Yamanaka factors (OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, c-MYC) or safer substitutes
small-molecule epigenetic modulators (e.g. DNA methyltransferase inhibitors, histone deacetylase inhibitors)
stabilizers to preserve activity in formulation

subsystems.name: Delivery vehicle
subsystems.role: carries the payload through the skin barrier to reach epidermal stem cells and fibroblasts.
parts: cream or gel base for topical application

subsystems.name: Targeting and control
subsystems.role: ensures only skin cells are affected and that reprogramming remains partial, not full.
parts: feedback sensors to halt reprogramming after a set time

subsystems.name: Safety switch
subsystems.role: prevents uncontrolled cell growth, teratoma formation or cancer.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and validation
subsystems.role: confirms that epigenetic age has been reset without harmful changes.

buildSteps.title: Map aging epigenome in skin
buildSteps.detail: Compare methylation patterns of young and old human skin cells to identify specific marks that change with age.

buildSteps.title: Select reprogramming cocktail
buildSteps.detail: Screen Yamanaka factors and small molecules for their ability to reverse those marks in cultured skin cells without inducing pluripotency.

buildSteps.title: Formulate for topical delivery
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate the active ingredients in nanoparticles or peptides that penetrate the stratum corneum and reach the epidermis and dermis.

buildSteps.title: Test on human skin equivalents
buildSteps.detail: Apply the formulation to lab-grown skin models and measure epigenetic age reversal, cell proliferation and toxicity.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate in animal models
buildSteps.detail: Test on mice or pigs for safety, efficacy and whether treated skin shows reduced scarring or improved wound healing without tumours.

buildSteps.title: Optimize dose and control
buildSteps.detail: Tune the dose and duration to achieve partial reprogramming only, using built-in safety switches to avoid cancer.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Phase I safety trials in humans, then Phase II/III trials for indications such as scar removal or skin rejuvenation.

buildSteps.title: Scale manufacturing and regulation
buildSteps.detail: Develop GMP production of the formulation, secure regulatory approval and launch as a cosmetic or therapeutic product.

prerequisites.why: shown in mice to reverse aspects of aging, but not yet achieved safely or in human skin.
lipid nanoparticles and peptides can carry cargo into skin, but delivery of large reprogramming factors to specific cell layers remains difficult.

prerequisites.tech: Control of reprogramming to avoid cancer
prerequisites.why: full reprogramming can cause teratomas; reliable partial and reversible control in human tissue is not yet demonstrated.
methylation-based age estimators exist and can measure whether a treatment resets epigenetic age.

pathway.milestone: lab research on partial reprogramming in mice and human cell cultures
pathway.unlocks: identification of safe factor combinations and delivery methods.

pathway.milestone: proof of concept in human skin explants and animal models
pathway.unlocks: evidence that topical reset can reverse epigenetic age without side effects.
data on dosing, tolerability and early efficacy signals.

pathway.milestone: approved topical products for scar removal or skin rejuvenation
pathway.unlocks: commercial availability, initially as cosmetics and later as therapies.
